name: key-facts
title: key-facts
description: A row of stated figures: each one a value with its label above and an optional qualifier beneath, on a bordered surface. Wraps to as many rows as the figures need. Owns its full style, references tokens only.

definition.name: key-facts
definition.description: A row of stated figures: each one a value with its label above and an optional qualifier beneath, on a bordered surface. Wraps to as many rows as the figures need. Owns its full style, references tokens only.
definition.whenToUse: Two to four figures the source states plainly, which a reader would compare at a glance, such as an allowance, a duration and a limit. One figure alone belongs in the sentence it came from. A wall of tiles reads as a dashboard, not a document.

facts.description: The figures, in the order the source states them. Every value is quoted from the source, never calculated, converted or rounded, and never invented to fill the row out.

label.description: What the figure counts, in the source's own words. Two or three words.

value.description: The figure exactly as the source states it, with its unit or symbol: '18%', 'SAR 750', '29 million'. Never a phrase, never a clause. Move a modifier like 'more than' or 'up to' into the qualifier rather than shortening the figure to fit: a truncated number is WRONG, where a longer qualifier is merely longer.

qualifier.description: The condition or period the figure carries, short. Empty when the source attaches none. It must be a COMPLETE phrase: if it will not fit, drop words until it does ('ATMs worldwide'), never stop mid-phrase ('ATMs and financial institutions within the King').
